1 · The question

Does the target rest on the owner?
Definition in use: gravity-resting contact on the supporter. Not proximity, not overlap, not "above". A cushion on a sofa qualifies; a picture hanging over a table does not, however close it is.

The two pairs highlighted green are ones you have already confirmed. They are shown so the sheet is self-consistent — leave or change them as you see fit.

2 · Pairs to judge

pink = the target (the thing that might be resting) · teal = the owner (what it might rest on) · grey = the rest of the room, ceiling clipped. The side-on view is the one to judge from: resting contact is a vertical question and the room views flatten it.

The evidence line is evidence, not a suggestion. One pair the algorithm proposes and one it rejects are both known-good, so it cannot be used as a shortcut.
